name: Pelikan Hi-Vis Safety Shell
description:
There is nothing subtle about this jacket and that is entirely the point. The Pelikan Hi-Vis Safety Shell is a Class 3 high-visibility rain jacket in ANSI-equivalent fluorescent yellow-green, with retroreflective silver tape at the chest, back, and arms in the standard chevron pattern. It is a lightweight shell, wind- and water-resistant, with a mesh lining and a hood that adjusts with a single cord. The Pelikan logo is small and on the chest. Everything else is light.

This is the jacket of infrastructure workers, road crews, site safety monitors, and dock workers across the Great Lakes corridor. It is also worn by anyone who needs to be seen in the dark — Shelf residents navigating dangerous transit routes sometimes wear hi-vis ironically or earnestly, as visibility is survival in certain parts of the city. Pelikan makes good shells at a working price. The reflective tape on this model catches light from a hundred meters.
what_it_says: You work outside or in hazardous conditions, or you have decided that being seen is more important than being fashionable. In the right context, this is also a kind of uniform.
worn_by: people who want to be visible in low light
story_hooks: A character uses a Pelikan hi-vis to move through a Shelf construction zone without challenge — workers in hi-vis are invisible in plain sight
Someone is using the reflective tape pattern to send coded signals; different tape configurations on different workers form a message visible from a drone overhead
A Tier 5 fashion label releases a runway piece clearly inspired by the Pelikan hi-vis; the infrastructure workers whose uniform it copies find this both flattering and enraging
